explanation: Meiosis II takes place in both cells produced during meiosis I and is not preceded by a round of DNA replication. Depending on the species, it begins either after the nuclear membrane re-forms or immediately after cytokinesis I. In Prophase II, spindle fibers form and move chromosomes toward the midline. In Metaphase II, chromosomes align at the midline, with sister chromatids facing opposite poles. During Anaphase II, chromatids separate and are pulled to opposite poles. In Telophase II, a nuclear membrane re-forms around the chromosomes in each of the four new cells. Finally, Cytokinesis II splits the cytoplasm, resulting in four completely separate haploid (1n) daughter cells from the original diploid (2n) parent cell.

questions.q: Does DNA replication occur before Meiosis II begins?
opts: Yes, DNA replicates to ensure the cells are diploid.
No, Meiosis II is not preceded by DNA replication.
Yes, but only in eukaryotic plant cells.
Yes, but only in somatic body cells.
